## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured their place in the final through a dominant display of offensive volume. They generated an average of 65.5 attacks per game, placing them at the 97th percentile against both that season's teams and all Champions League clubs since 2011-12. This relentless pressure was supported by 13.2 shots per game (97th percentile) and a high volume of passing with 656 passes per game (94th percentile). Their defensive solidity also played a crucial role, as they allowed just 6.0 opponent shots per game, ranking in the 6th percentile where lower is better. These factors culminated in a historic final victory where they beat Inter 5-0 to become the winner of the tournament.

## Would the model have picked them?
The predictive model would likely have selected Paris Saint-Germain as a strong contender despite their actual performance not being seen during training. The model assigned them a 10.1% probability of reaching the final, which is notably higher than the base rate of 8.3% for any random knockout team. This elevated confidence placed them at rank 8 among the season's 24 knockout teams based on that probability. While their expected knockout stage score was only 0.82—suggesting a model expectation closer to the quarter-finals—their high offensive metrics pushed the prediction upward significantly, indicating the model recognized their potential for deep runs even if it underestimated the final outcome.

## Weak spots
Despite their success, specific statistical areas held the team back from an even higher predicted rank. The most significant drag came from a low reliance on long passes at 9.1% of total passes, a figure ranking in just the 7th percentile historically. Additionally, while their defense was strong overall, their goal difference per game was only 0.62 (69th percentile), and they committed fouls at a rate of 9.4 per game (12th percentile). Their shot accuracy was also a concern at 46.2% on target (36th percentile), and their shot conversion sat at just 13.2% (41st percentile). These inefficiencies in finishing and tactical variety prevented the model from ranking them higher, even as they managed to overcome these limitations to win the title.
